From the wheel

The maker's process

Nothing here is mass-produced. Every piece passes through the same slow sequence of hands, heat, and time.

i.

Throwing

We wedge local stoneware and throw each form on the wheel — centring, opening, and pulling the walls until the shape feels right in the hand.

ii.

Trimming & drying

Once leather-hard, each piece is trimmed, footed, and left to dry slowly before its first bisque firing to a stable, porous state.

iii.

Glaze & fire

We mix our own muted glazes and fire to 1240°C. The kiln has the final word — small variations are kept, not corrected.
